results.content:
Title: Should I upgrade to the "mainline" kernels? - Ask Ubuntu
#### Stack Exchange Network. Stack Exchange network consists of 183 Q&A communities including Stack Overflow, the largest, most trusted online community for developers to learn, share their knowledge, and build their careers. ### your communities. ### more stack exchange communities. Stack Overflow for Teams is now called **Stack Internal**. # Should I upgrade to the "mainline" kernels? Newer "mainline" versions of the kernel are available from the Ubuntu kernel team, e.g. 3.4 and 3.5, while Ubuntu 12.04 is on 3.2. # Upgrading to a mainline kernel is usually *not* a good idea. Most of the basic information in this answer is from the Mainline Builds wiki. They are provided only for testing and are unsupported. You should only install these if you believe they may fix a critical problem you are having with the current kernel. If you install a mainline or other newer kernel, you can still choose to use your old (stable) kernel by selecting it at boot-time:. User the down arrow to go to "Previous Linux Versions" and press `Enter`. This is usually the first option unless you have installed multiple mainline/custom kernels. Instead of mainline, you should consider LTS enablement stack. Where, a newer kernel / graphics stack is backported officially, only for LTS Ubuntu releases. If you know of a specific fix or improvement in how the newer kernel handles your hardware, I say go for it. I would not have upgraded to a mainline kernel due to lack of support, except that I was having some trouble with N64 game emulation running very sluggishly with lots of bugs. This was enough to motivate me to test it and the results in appearance and performance were amazing with no new problems arising as of yet. One thing to note is whether you have external modules (aka out-of-tree) installed (see Indentify out of tree modules to get an idea where these are). If you need these modules, consider whether they will build against the new kernel version. It is recommended to remove external or proprietary modules before attempting to upgrade to the mainline kernel.
